scenes.title: Systems Manager Managed Node Prerequisites
scenes.narration: The final slide examines the conditions required before Systems Manager can manage a node. Start with an EC2 instance or a supported hybrid machine. The SSM Agent must be installed at an appropriate version and running, but the agent alone is not enough. EC2 typically uses an instance IAM role with the required Systems Manager permissions; a hybrid activation uses the relevant managed-node identity configuration. The machine also needs outbound HTTPS connectivity to the applicable Systems Manager endpoints, either through suitable network egress or private VPC endpoints with working DNS and security groups. The diagram names SSM and message endpoints, with other service endpoints needed for particular features and Regions. Once the prerequisites are satisfied, Fleet Manager and Systems Manager functions can run operational commands, collect inventory and support patch workflows. If a machine appears offline, inspect IAM identity, endpoint routing, proxy and DNS configuration, then agent health and logs. Do not automatically conclude the agent is broken. For GenAI infrastructure, this managed access pattern can reduce reliance on inbound SSH while supporting repeatable patching and configuration. It still needs tightly scoped operator permissions and audit logging.
